citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
There have been several incidences where medication for covered animals was used, not used, or substituted, that
differed from the protocol as submitted and approved.
**On Feb 17, 2026, four (4) Rhesus Macaques were anesthetized for CT scan and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), where
they received sterile 50% dextrose solution instead of sterile 0.9% saline. While this triggered additional monitoring by
veterinary staff, animals were stable and suffered no effects.
**Feb 10-12, 2026, two (2) rabbits did not receive the pre-operative glycopyrrolate injection that was part of the approved
protocol. No adverse event resulted from the medication omission.
**Sept. 8-18, 2025, three (3) rabbits received a commercially available catheter locking solution that was not included in
the protocol for use. No animal welfare concerns were found.
**On Aug. 24, 2025, one (1) African green monkey was administered a medication via intramuscular route, when only
intravenous or subcutaneous routes were approved. The animal underwent extended monitoring and no adverse event
resulted from the incorrect administration route.
Failure to secure IACUC approval for modifications to an approved protocol prior to enacting those changes does not
afford the IACUC the opportunity to review the changes regarding the care and use of animals in ongoing activities and
either approve, require modifications in, or withhold approval of the changes. Performing activities not covered by IACUC-
approved protocols can also result in harm or death to the impacted animals.
With respect to activities involving animals, the IACUC, as an agent of the research facility, shall: review and approve,
require modification in (to secure approval), or withhold approval or proposed significant changes regarding the care and
use of animals in ongoing activities.
These incidents were identified by the facility prior to inspection and corrective measures were implemented.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
